# Dashboard keyboard accessibility fixes for the four audited core flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard accessibility defects identified by the
accessibility audit in the four core Dashboard flows: project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission. It delivers
full keyboard operability of these flows — no focus traps and no unreachable
controls — and consistent, visible focus indicators across them. The Dashboard
is the platform's existing single-pane web console; all fixes extend its
existing UI code.

## Scope

- Fix focus loss in modals and overlays across the four audited flows: focus
  must enter and exit every modal correctly and return to the triggering
  control on dismissal.
- Make every interactive control in the four audited flows reachable and
  operable by keyboard alone (Tab, Shift+Tab, arrow keys, Enter, Space, Esc
  as applicable).
- Resolve every defect enumerated in the audit report for the four flows.
- Apply consistent, visible focus indicators across all controls in the
  audited flows.
- Stay within the audited scope: no screen-reader semantics beyond what the
  keyboard fixes require, and no changes to flows outside the four audited
  ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model
  deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed end-to-end using
  keyboard input alone — measured by a manual walkthrough of each flow
  completed without a pointing device.
- Every defect enumerated in the audit report is resolved or explicitly
  dispositioned with rationale.
- No focus traps remain: focus can move into and out of every modal and
  overlay in the audited flows, and returns to the triggering control when
  dismissed.
- All interactive controls in the audited flows are keyboard-reachable and
  keyboard-operable.
- Focus indicators are visible and consistent across all controls in the
  four audited flows.
- Pointer-based operation of the audited flows is not regressed — existing
  mouse-driven workflows still pass.
- No changes are made to screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard
  fixes require, and no changes to flows outside the four audited ones.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)** — the four audited core flows fully operable by keyboard,
  with no focus traps or unreachable controls: fully covered by this epic.
- **HLR-2 (P1)** — visible focus indicators consistent across the audited
  flows: fully covered by this epic. HLR-1 and HLR-2 share the same
  implementation surface (focus handling across the same four flows) and are
  therefore bundled rather than split.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement)

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation
to reflect the fixed keyboard-accessibility state of the four audited
Dashboard flows: the VPAT (accessibility conformance report) and the product
documentation accessibility statement. Both documents must accurately
describe the post-fix behavior, pass technical review against the implemented
fixes, and be republished to their live locations. This is a docs content
deliverable that two public-sector customers require ahead of renewal; it
depends on the keyboard accessibility fixes being complete, because the
documentation describes and is verified against the implemented behavior.

## Scope

- Update the VPAT / accessibility conformance report to reflect the keyboard
  operability and focus-indicator conformance state of the four audited flows
  after the fixes.
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to reflect the
  fixed state.
- Technically review the updated documents against the implemented fixes so
  that every conformance claim is verified against actual product behavior.
- Republish both documents to their live published locations.
- Limit conformance claims to the strategy's scope (the four audited flows,
  keyboard operability and focus indicators); do not claim conformance for
  out-of-scope areas such as screen-reader semantics or unaudited flows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT is updated to accurately reflect the post-fix keyboard conformance
  state of the four audited flows.
- The product documentation accessibility statement is updated to reflect
  the fixed state.
- The updated conformance documentation is technically reviewed against the
  implemented keyboard fixes before publication — every conformance claim is
  verified against actual product behavior (per HLR-3's technical-review
  requirement and the docs-authoring review rule).
- The updated VPAT and accessibility statement are republished and live at
  their published locations.
- No conformance claims are made beyond the strategy's scope: screen-reader
  semantics beyond the keyboard fixes and flows outside the four audited
  ones are not claimed as conformant.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2)** — the accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and
  product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to
  reflect the fixed state, with technical review: fully covered by this
  epic.
